מיטב "עוקב מדדי מניות" מציג 25.86% ב-3 שנים ו-17.25% ב-5, עם דמי ניהול של 0.65%, והוא הטוב ביותר עד כה ל-5 שנים. "אלטשולר שחם" חדש במסלול ה-S&P 500 (פחות מ-3 שנים), לכן אין בו הרבה מה לראות, ואני ממשיך לסרוק את היתר.

content.text:
The "עוד לא דווח" with an orange "!" next to the fee feels like a warning. I'd skip those.
"כלל" I know, the insurance company.

I'd go with **מיטב, the "עוקב מדדי מניות" track**. I'm fairly sure, honestly. What decided it: it shows "25.86%" over 3 years and "17.25%" over 5, the best 5-year number I saw, and מיטב is a name I know from ads. That's like 17% a year, so in 5 years my 30,000 would be about 55,000. The fee is "0.65%", which is small.

Second choice was אנליסט "עוקב מדדים - גמיש" ("26.39%" / "15.37%"), but מיטב is the bigger name. The S&P 500 tracks my friends talk about are only about 13% at every company, which seems worse.

First step? No idea. There's no button to join, only arrows on each row.

**How it went:**
- **What I looked at:** It opened on "קופת גמל להשקעה" already picked, so that was good. Then I scrolled the long table company by company: the first one (no name I could see), מור, אנליסט, מיטב, אלטשולר שחם, one more without a name, ילין לפידות, כלל, מנורה מבטחים, אינפיניטי, איילון.
- **What I skipped:** The text under the heading, the orange notice box, and the filter chips (except noticing the S&P one). Also the grey note at the bottom and the footer. I didn't touch the search box or open any row arrows.
- **Words I didn't get:** "מט"ח" next to the circles, and what the circles even are. "עוד לא דווח" with the orange "!". "מההפקדות" vs "מההחיסכון". "101%" מניות, which makes no sense to me. "נכסים". Lots of rows say "פחות מ־3 שנים", so I couldn't compare them.
- **What bugged me:**
  - The company names sit on a grey line in the middle of the table. Once that scrolls past, you don't know whose rows you're looking at. That happened to me twice, including the very first company.
  - It's 143 rows of the same track names, over and over. By ילין לפידות I was bored and only went to the end to see if there was a bottom line. There wasn't one: no "best for you" and no next step.
  - All the fees are 0.5–0.7%, so they all look the same. I couldn't tell what that means in shekels.
